text: Add impression-time request-context features tab, hour, and weekday to the neutral user/video additive scorer while leaving model, loss, and training unchanged.
rationale: The only screened feature group with positive overall primary lift and full coverage is request context, but its modest size and daily variability require confirmation.
exact_ablation: Add only the request-context feature group {tab, hour, weekday}; keep the neutral additive architecture, BCE objective, optimizer, and schedule fixed.

expected_effect.GAUC: Likely small positive lift from improved broad within-user ordering, especially for warm users/items; expect approximately +0.001 to +0.004.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: Possible small positive or neutral effect because screening showed weaker top-five concentration; expect approximately -0.001 to +0.003.

text: Add only tab as an impression-time categorical feature to the neutral additive user/video scorer.
rationale: Tab is a single, fully available request-context field and isolates whether part of the measured request-context gain comes from placement or surface differences.
exact_ablation: Add only the tab feature; exclude hour and weekday and keep every model, loss, and training setting unchanged.

expected_effect.GAUC: Likely small positive or neutral effect from surface-specific within-user ordering; expect approximately 0.000 to +0.003.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: Likely neutral to mildly positive, with a plausible effect of 0.000 to +0.002.

text: Add only impression-time hour and weekday features to the neutral additive user/video scorer.
rationale: Temporal request context produced positive lifts on three of four screened days, making a time-context-only confirmation a useful decomposition of the aggregate request-context result.
exact_ablation: Add only hour and weekday; do not add tab and do not change architecture, loss, optimizer, or schedule.

expected_effect.GAUC: Likely positive but time-regime dependent; expect approximately +0.001 to +0.004.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: Likely neutral to mildly positive, with possible instability across time blocks; expect approximately -0.001 to +0.003.

text: Replace the neutral additive ID scorer with an embedding-plus-MLP scorer using the same user_id and video_id inputs only.
rationale: The seed has only additive ID effects, so compact embeddings and a nonlinear trunk could model user-item affinity patterns without introducing any additional feature family.
exact_ablation: Replace only the additive linear scoring architecture with a user/video embedding-plus-MLP architecture; retain the same IDs, BCE loss, data split, and training budget.

expected_effect.GAUC: Potential moderate positive lift if nonlinear identity interactions matter; expect approximately +0.001 to +0.008.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: Potential positive lift at the top ranks, but greater variance from overfitting; expect approximately -0.002 to +0.008.

text: Replace the neutral additive scorer with a low-rank Deep & Cross architecture using the same user_id and video_id inputs.
rationale: Explicit bounded-order crosses target candidate-specific user-item interactions while retaining a relatively compact architecture and avoiding unsafe metadata or outcome fields.
exact_ablation: Replace only the additive architecture with a two-layer low-rank cross network over user/video embeddings; keep features, BCE loss, optimizer, and schedule fixed.

expected_effect.GAUC: Could improve broad within-user discrimination if explicit identity crosses help; expect approximately -0.002 to +0.007.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: Could improve top-five ordering but may be volatile for sparse IDs; expect approximately -0.003 to +0.007.

text: Replace pointwise BCE with a BCE plus nDCG@5-weighted within-group pairwise ranking loss while retaining the neutral additive scorer and current inputs.
rationale: The screened request-context group improved broad ranking more than top-five concentration, so directly weighting swaps affecting the first five positions is a materially different route to improve nDCG@5.
exact_ablation: Replace only the pointwise BCE objective with the specified BCE-plus-LambdaRank-style nDCG@5 hybrid; keep architecture, features, optimizer, and sampling unchanged.

expected_effect.GAUC: Likely neutral to mildly negative because optimization focuses on top-five swaps; expect approximately -0.003 to +0.002.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: Most likely positive if displayed groups are reconstructed correctly; expect approximately +0.001 to +0.008.

text: Replace shuffled minibatch training with deterministic chronological minibatch training over the same neutral additive model and features.
rationale: A chronological training order can reduce optimization mismatch under temporal drift without adding any feature or changing the model objective.
exact_ablation: Change only the training minibatch order from seeded random permutation to chronological order; retain architecture, features, BCE loss, learning rate, and epoch budget.

expected_effect.GAUC: Likely neutral, with a possible small positive effect if temporal drift is material; expect approximately -0.002 to +0.003.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: Likely neutral to mildly positive or negative depending on recency bias; expect approximately -0.002 to +0.003.

text: Increase the neutral additive model's embedding-free ID regularization from the seed value to a stronger fixed L2 penalty.
rationale: The current scaffold can memorize sparse user/video effects; stronger regularization is a cheap, isolated test for whether generalization rather than capacity is limiting ranking quality.
exact_ablation: Change only L2 regularization from 1e-6 to 1e-4; keep IDs, additive architecture, BCE loss, optimizer, and all other configuration fixed.

expected_effect.GAUC: Likely neutral to mildly positive if sparse-ID overfitting exists, otherwise slightly negative; expect approximately -0.003 to +0.002.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: Likely neutral or mildly positive through smoother scores; expect approximately -0.003 to +0.002.

text: Remove user_id from the neutral additive scorer, leaving video_id as the sole predictive input.
rationale: This is a clean diagnostic of whether user-specific variation is helping within-user ordering; it is expected to be a fallback or negative control rather than a likely winner.
exact_ablation: Remove only user_id; retain video_id, additive scoring, BCE loss, optimizer, and schedule unchanged.

expected_effect.GAUC: Likely negative because user-specific ordering information is removed; expect approximately -0.010 to -0.001.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: Likely negative or neutral, especially for users exposed to heterogeneous items; expect approximately -0.010 to +0.001.

text: Remove video_id from the neutral additive scorer, leaving user_id as the sole predictive input.
rationale: A user-only constant cannot change within-user item ordering, making this a concrete sanity-control ablation for the ranking task.
exact_ablation: Remove only video_id; retain user_id, additive scoring, BCE loss, optimizer, and schedule unchanged.

expected_effect.GAUC: Expected to collapse toward tie behavior and decrease substantially because scores become constant within user; expect approximately -0.10 to -0.01.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: Expected to decrease substantially from loss of candidate differentiation; expect approximately -0.10 to -0.01.

text: Add only server_width and server_height as normalized impression-time numeric context features to the neutral additive scorer.
rationale: Display dimensions are available request context and provide an isolated test of device/layout effects distinct from the measured tab-hour-weekday group.
exact_ablation: Add only server_width and server_height; exclude tab, hour, and weekday and keep architecture, loss, optimizer, and schedule unchanged.

expected_effect.GAUC: Likely neutral to mildly positive if layout context changes long-view propensity within users; expect approximately -0.001 to +0.003.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: Likely neutral or very small positive because the signal may shift calibration more than relative item ordering; expect approximately -0.001 to +0.002.

text: Add only one-hot categorical context fields onehot_feat0 through onehot_feat17 to the neutral additive scorer, with separate learned weights and unknown buckets.
rationale: The one-hot fields are available candidate/impression attributes and offer a broader but still single-family alternative to the measured request-context group without using metadata snapshots or outcomes.
exact_ablation: Add only the one-hot feature family {onehot_feat0..onehot_feat17}; keep user_id/video_id, additive architecture, BCE loss, optimizer, and schedule fixed.

expected_effect.GAUC: Potential small positive lift if these fields encode contextual preference differences, but sparse categories may add noise; expect approximately -0.003 to +0.004.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: Likely neutral to mildly positive with higher variance than the compact request-context group; expect approximately -0.003 to +0.004.
